items.title: Mighty Darkwave Duo Deathday Returns with Venemous New Single “Hungry Ghosts”
items.summary: The rain falls down an endless sound… In the early 2010s, there was truly no band I liked better than Deathday. Formerly known as Deathday Party and centered around brothers… The post Mighty Darkwave Duo Deathday Returns with Venemous New Single “Hungry Ghosts
items.fullText:
The rain falls down
an endless sound… 

In the early 2010s, there was truly no band I liked better than Deathday. Formerly known as Deathday Party and centered around brothers and multi-instrumentalists Alex and Giovanni Guillén, the band walked a fine line between controlled experimental chaos and furious club bangers, often exploring both sides of the cold/dark post-punk spectrum on the same track. The duo released two LPs, several singles, and a handful of killer compilation tracks (including the absolutely lethal “Dropped Into Obscurity,” a track we selected as our personal best of the decade) before going on hiatus, with Alex working primarily as DJ, producer, and film composer since.

However, after over a decade of silence, Deathday has returned with an equally lethal new single, titled “Hungry Ghosts.” The track is the first taste of new music from upcoming LP Sans Soleil and was recorded and produced alongside the legendary Matia Simovich at Infinite Power Studios in LA. The track is a welcome breath of fresh air, the sound of true masters of the genre picking back up where they left off. All the ingredients that made Deathday my personal favorite band of the era are back in full effect, including razor sharp production, scathing guitars, textured vocals, and whirling synthesizers, with a delightful Cure-inspired guitar solo that takes flight towards the end of the track. “Hungry Ghosts” is a truly triumph of the genre, a modern day masterpiece that pleases and devastates in all the best ways.

Listen to the track below:

The track’s origins stem from a cleverly reversed instrumental loop, which serves as the ominous backbone of the track and taps into the band’s surrealist influences which include Jean Cocteau, Ingmar Bergman, and of course, David Lynch, as well as a variety of literary and sonic touchstones that are meant to displace the senses. Giovanni Guillén explains, “We write a lot from the unconscious, surrealist perspective of a person, place, or atmosphere. Characters that aren’t all there. Realities that shift and turn.”

“Hungry Ghosts” is out today on Bandcamp and all streaming services. Stay tuned for more from the band and upcoming release details for Sans Soleil.

items.title: vidnaObmana’s ‘The River Of Appearance’ turns 30
items.summary: Projekt Records marked 30 years of vidnaObmana's ambient album 'The River Of Appearance' with a new Dirk Serries interview on Opus Zine.
items.fullText:
Projekt Records marked the 30th anniversary of vidnaObmana’s ambient album “The River Of Appearance”, originally released in 1996, with a new interview in which Opus Zine’s Jason Morehead spoke to Belgian composer Dirk Serries about the album’s recording, its 2006 rework by Oregon ensemble Dreams In Exile, and its Zoharum 25th-anniversary edition. The interview, “30 Years of Serenity: Dirk Serries Reflects on vidnaObmana’s The River of Appearance”, is available on Opus Zine.

“The River Of Appearance” consists of eight pieces built around sparse piano lines, drifting keyboard loops and organic rainstick sounds. Alternative Press critic Bryan Reesman described it at the time as music in which “sparse, pretty piano lines float over shimmering walls of electronics, evoking a melancholic yet romantic feeling,” with “cyclical melodies” interweaving “in a slowly moving stream of sound.”

“The River Of Appearance” is available as a name-your-price digital album, and as a 10th-anniversary 2CD edition (which adds a disc of the album reinterpreted on traditional instruments by Dreams In Exile) for $15, both on Bandcamp.

About vidnaObmana

vidnaObmana was the primary recording name of Belgian composer Dirk Serries, used across a body of ambient and dark ambient work that included “The River Of Appearance” in 1996. Projekt Records released a 10th-anniversary edition of the album in 2006, pairing the original with a reinterpretation by Oregon ensemble Dreams In Exile performed on traditional instruments; a 25th-anniversary edition followed on the Polish label Zoharum.

Side-Line has previously covered Serries’ work on the 1992 vidnaObmana album “Terrace of Memories”, remastered in collaboration with Projekt founder Sam Rosenthal, including the Kickstarter campaign that funded its physical formats.

Thirty years on, “The River Of Appearance” remains part of Projekt’s active catalogue, with the new Opus Zine interview placing the album’s recording and its various reissues in Serries’ own words.

items.title: Phil Stiles announces double EP ‘I’m Fading’
items.summary: Final Coil frontman Phil Stiles announced the double EP 'I'm Fading', out 11 December 2026 on Nyctophobic Records, with a video premiered on 13 November.
items.fullText:
Final Coil frontman and songwriter Phil Stiles announced a new double EP, “I’m Fading”, set for release on 11 December 2026 via Nyctophobic Records. It is his first original solo material since 2021; this year’s “Plaid and Lead” was a reworking of Matt Steady’s “Velvet and Gold” album rather than new original material.

The title track and first single was released alongside its video on 13 November 2026, viewable on YouTube.

The first disc, the four-track “I’m Fading EP”, features three new tracks recorded with Chris Barber (Crazy Town) on drums, plus a remix of the title track by Seattle-based producer Shane Aungst. The second disc, “Thornhill’s Night Out EP”, is built around electronica, moving from influences including The Orb, Leftfield, Orbital and The Chemical Brothers toward the more abstract sound of Aphex Twin, and closes with a Shane Aungst remix of The Anchorhold’s “Dance Fucker”.

“I’m Fading” will be released as a limited-edition double CD featuring artwork and photography by Final Coil’s Jola Stiles, alongside standalone digital releases on Phil Stiles’ Bandcamp page.

Disc 1, “I’m Fading EP”: “I’m Fading”; “Uprooted”; “Filtered”; “I’m Fading” (Shane Aungst Remix).

Disc 2, “Thornhill’s Night Out EP”: “Dead of the Night”; “Bliss”; “Wiped Out”; “Chemikalized”; “Keep Your Head Down”; “The Walls Gleam in the Darkness”; “Lost in the Aether”; “Dance Fucker” (Shane Aungst Remix).

About Phil Stiles

Phil Stiles is the frontman and songwriter of Final Coil, a project previously covered by Side-Line, including Shane Aungst’s 2022 remix album “The Anchorhold Dissolution”, based on Stiles’ own studio material.

Earlier in 2026, Stiles released “Plaid and Lead”, a reworking of Matt Steady’s “Velvet and Gold” album. “I’m Fading” marks his return to original solo songwriting, drawing on the harder-edged alternative and progressive sound of Final Coil alongside the more electronic, post-punk-leaning material that makes up the second disc.

items.title: Kim Lunner releases new single ‘I Know’
items.summary: Norwegian electronic artist Kim Lunner released the single 'I Know' on Town And Towers Records on 13 November 2026, addressing childhood insecurity.
items.fullText:
Norwegian electronic music producer Kim Lunner released the single “I Know” on 13 November 2026 through Town And Towers Records. The song addresses the contrast between childhood dreams of a secure life and a reality in which, for some children, that security remains out of reach.

Lunner describes the track in his own words: “‘I Know’ is a song about children who dream of something new – freedom, love, and security. But the truth is that it is only a dream. They live in a society where a sense of insecurity is only growing. Stepping out of the shadows and having a home of their own, with a family, remains nothing more than a dream.”

“I Know” is available to stream and buy on Bandcamp, and on major streaming services via orcd.co/iknow__.

About Kim Lunner

Kim Lunner is a Norwegian music producer who has been making music since 2011. He released his first album on 20 May 2020 through Scent Air Records, and began singing on his own recordings that same year. Following the label change prompted by the war in Ukraine, Lunner signed in 2022 with the Danish label Town And Towers Records.

Originally a drummer, Lunner produces his own drum parts and favours slower tempos built around synthesizer patterns, blending synthpop, futurepop and electro with darker electronic textures. His catalogue now runs to more than 25 singles, four EPs and five albums.

In 2023, Lunner joined the Norwegian futurepop band Supercraft, and co-founded the electronic project State of Anguish with fellow Norwegian synth artist Egil Thoms Hansen. Side-Line previously covered Lunner’s 2025 single “With You” and Supercraft’s 2024 reissue of “Select & Operate”.

“I Know” follows that run of releases as Lunner’s latest single under his own name on Town And Towers Records.

items.title: Vlimmer releases new album ‘Kiemenatmung’
items.summary: Berlin darkgaze project Vlimmer released the twelve-track album 'Kiemenatmung' on Blackjack Illuminist Records on 13 November 2026, its sixth full-length.
items.fullText:
Berlin-based darkgaze project Vlimmer released its sixth full-length album, “Kiemenatmung”, on 13 November 2026 via Blackjack Illuminist Records. The twelve-track album is the work of Berlin musician Alexander Leonard Donat, who also runs the label.

The title translates as “gill breathing”, the way fish extract oxygen from water, used on the album as a metaphor for rising deadlines, shifting relationships and mounting anxiety. Donat describes the record as resilience shown through endurance, not triumph, with water imagery of diving under, resurfacing and swimming against invisible currents running through all twelve songs.

Musically, “Kiemenatmung” continues Vlimmer’s blend of post-punk and darkwave, folding in shoegaze guitar textures. According to the label, tracks including “Atemdauer”, “Lockenkopf” and “Besitzergreifung” lean toward techno, while “Augendrang” and “Wasserstand” move into melancholic wave-pop. The album closes with “Lavalunge”, in which the record’s water imagery gives way to fire.

“Kiemenatmung” is available as a name-your-price digital album on Bandcamp.

About Vlimmer

Alexander Leonard Donat founded Blackjack Illuminist Records in Berlin and has released Vlimmer’s music through it ever since, across singles, EPs and now six full-length albums under a self-described “darkgaze” label spanning post-punk and darkwave, with shoegaze and industrial textures layered in.

Side-Line has tracked Vlimmer’s output across several releases, including the 2021 Nirvana cover compilation “Nevermind Reworks”, the 2022 two-track single “Noposition/1979”, the 2023 album “Zerschöpfung”, and, most recently, “Augendrang”, released in October 2026 as the final single ahead of “Kiemenatmung”.

With “Kiemenatmung” now out in full, that single’s b-side cover of The Bangles’ “Eternal Flame” and the “Augendrang” single both take their place within the complete twelve-track album.

items.title: Agent Side Grinder release single ‘The Choir’ on Metropolis Records
items.summary: Agent Side Grinder released 'The Choir' on Metropolis Records on 13 November 2026, their first new single since 2023 and a signing to the US label.
items.fullText:
Swedish electronic post-punk trio Agent Side Grinder released the single “The Choir” on 13 November 2026 via Metropolis Records. It is the band’s first new original single since “Jack Vegas” (2023) and their first release on the American label following their signing to it.

“The Choir” was produced by Jimmy Monell, who has also worked with Kite and Emmon, and was recorded at Agent Side Grinder’s own studio in northwestern Stockholm. The track addresses the power of words and how quickly they can spread, multiply and take on a life of their own.

Agent Side Grinder have also announced a new EP for March 2027, which the band say will eventually form part of a double EP release.

European tour with Then Comes Silence in January 2027

Agent Side Grinder will join fellow Swedish band and Metropolis Records labelmates Then Comes Silence for eight co-headlining European dates in January 2027, with further live activity planned for spring 2027.

Tour dates:

  • 8 January 2027 – Hamburg, Molotow (Germany)
  • 9 January 2027 – Detmold, Owls N Bats Festival (Germany)
  • 10 January 2027 – Oberhausen, Kulttempel (Germany)
  • 12 January 2027 – Chambéry, Brin de Zinc (France)
  • 13 January 2027 – Liège, Deux Ours (Belgium)
  • 14 January 2027 – Hannover, Lux (Germany)

About Agent Side Grinder

Agent Side Grinder formed in Stockholm in the late 2000s, founded by Peter Fristedt and Johan Lange. Vocalist Emanuel Åström joined the band in 2017, after which the group released the albums “A/X” (2019) and “Jack Vegas” (2023), developing a sound built on analogue electronics, driving rhythms and dark melodies within Sweden’s electronic post-punk scene.

Side-Line has previously covered the band’s back catalogue, including the first clear-vinyl pressing of ‘A/X’ in 2024, and Beborn Beton’s use of an Agent Side Grinder remix on their own single in 2025. The band’s influence has also reached younger acts, with groups such as Molchat Doma and Boy Harsher citing Agent Side Grinder as an influence.

“The Choir” is Agent Side Grinder’s first release under the Metropolis Records deal, ahead of the January 2027 tour with Then Comes Silence and the EP due in March 2027.

items.title: Silent Weapon releases third album ‘Oblivion Seeker’
items.summary: Oxford dark-electro project Silent Weapon releases its third album, "Oblivion Seeker," on Bandcamp, with guests Octavia Freud, Black Tish and Deeq.
items.fullText:
Oxford, UK dark-electro and industrial project Silent Weapon released its third album, “Oblivion Seeker,” on Bandcamp on 13 November 2026. The eight-track digital album features guest vocalists Octavia Freud, Black Tish and Deeq, with cover artwork by Zubair Chaudhry.

The tracklist opens with “Oppression Olympics,” featuring Octavia Freud, and runs through “Energy Vampire,” “False Equivalence” (featuring Black Tish), “Annihilation Terror,” “Second Class Citizen” (featuring Octavia Freud), “Happy Puppet” and “Jab Daddy & Captain Brainchip,” closing with “Top Down Control,” featuring Deeq.

“Oblivion Seeker” is available as a digital album on Bandcamp.

About Silent Weapon

Oxford-based musician Umair Chaudhry records as Silent Weapon, mixing dark-electro and industrial electronics with elements of noise. The project’s catalogue includes the releases “Eggshells,” “Purge,” “Purged,” “Demonology” and “Demonised,” along with the EP “Cognitive Dissonance.” Its 2023 EP, “The Fear Of The Possibility Of Chaos,” released on Blindsight Records on 10 November 2023, paired three original tracks with a cover of Voivod’s “Angel Rat” and was reviewed by Side-Line, which highlighted the tracks “Menticide” and the EP’s title track. “Oblivion Seeker,” Silent Weapon‘s third album, continues the project’s run of self-released dark-electro material, bringing in Octavia Freud, Black Tish and Deeq as guest vocalists across its eight tracks.

items.title: KÁRYYN reworks Depeche Mode’s ‘Survive’ for ‘Sunrise on the Reaping’ soundtrack
items.summary: Depeche Mode's "Survive" gets an Arena Mix reworked by KÁRYYN for "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" soundtrack, out 13 November 2026 on MCA.
items.fullText:
Depeche Mode‘s “Survive” appears in a new Arena Mix reworked by KÁRYYN on “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping (The Album),” released 13 November 2026 on MCA. The track, listed as “Survive (Arena Mix | KÁRYYN Rework),” is track 19 of the 29-track soundtrack and streams digitally from release day alongside double-CD and purple-vinyl double-LP gatefold editions.

Martin Gore and Dave Gahan wrote “Survive,” and James Ford produced the original version, recorded during the sessions for Depeche Mode’s 2023 studio album “Memento Mori.” The song later appeared as a bonus track on the band’s 2025 live album “Memento Mori: Mexico City,” alongside “Life 2.0,” “Give Yourself To Me” and “In The End.” For the Arena Mix, KÁRYYN reworked the track and added new vocal parts.

“The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping (The Album)” also features Kacey Musgraves, Stevie Nicks, The Smashing Pumpkins, Noah Kahan, Jennifer Lawrence and The Cure, who close the record. The soundtrack ties to the film “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping,” directed by Francis Lawrence and starring Joseph Zada as a young Haymitch Abernathy, which opens in cinemas on 20 November 2026, a week after the album.

About Depeche Mode

Formed in Basildon, Essex, in 1980, the band’s founding members were Vince Clarke, Martin Gore, Andy Fletcher and Dave Gahan. The band debuted with “Speak & Spell” in 1981, the only Depeche Mode album written primarily by Clarke, who left that year to form Yazoo and later Erasure. Gore became the band’s main songwriter from “A Broken Frame” (1982) onward. Alan Wilder joined in 1982 and remained a member through “Songs of Faith and Devotion” (1993), departing in 1995.

The band’s catalogue includes “Construction Time Again” (1983), “Some Great Reward” (1984), “Black Celebration” (1986), “Music for the Masses” (1987), “Violator” (1990), “Songs of Faith and Devotion” (1993), “Ultra” (1997), “Exciter” (2001), “Playing the Angel” (2005), “Sounds of the Universe” (2009), “Delta Machine” (2013), “Spirit” (2017) and “Memento Mori” (2023), the latter produced by James Ford and the first album made after Andy Fletcher’s death in May 2022. Depeche Mode now continues as the duo of Dave Gahan and Martin Gore, who in October also released a remixed version of “Cross Whisper” under the name MG x CD + JL = with Cliff Damavandi. The band’s three sold-out 2023 concerts at Mexico City’s Foro Sol Stadium on the Memento Mori World Tour were documented on the concert film and live album “Memento Mori: Mexico City,” whose bonus tracks include “Survive,” the song now reworked for the Hunger Games soundtrack.

items.title: New Order’s ‘Movement’ turns 45 on 13 November
items.summary: New Order released their debut album "Movement" through Factory Records on 13 November 1981. The album turns 45 this year.
items.fullText:
English post-punk band New Order released their debut studio album, “Movement,” through Factory Records on 13 November 1981. Martin Hannett produced the record. “Movement” turns 45 this year.

The band recorded “Movement” between 24 April and 4 May 1981 at Strawberry Studios in Stockport, with Chris Nagle engineering and John Leckie and Flood assisting. The sessions followed the end of Joy Division after singer Ian Curtis’s death in May 1980, and “Movement” was the first album the surviving trio of Bernard Sumner, Peter Hook and Stephen Morris made as New Order, now joined by keyboardist Gillian Gilbert. The album reached number 30 on the UK Albums Chart and number one on the UK Independent Albums Chart. No single was taken from the album.

The eight-track record runs 35 minutes and 20 seconds:

  1. “Dreams Never End”
  2. “Truth”
  3. “Senses”
  4. “Chosen Time”
  5. “ICB”
  6. “The Him”
  7. “Doubts Even Here”
  8. “Denial”

Sumner sang lead vocals, guitars, melodica and synthesisers; Hook played bass and sang lead on “Dreams Never End” and “Doubts Even Here”; Gilbert played synthesisers and guitars and spoke the words on “Doubts Even Here”; Morris played drums and synthesisers. Hook later described the record’s production as unsettled: “I actually liked Movement, but I know why nobody else likes it.” “Movement” streams on Spotify.

About New Order

New Order formed in Manchester in 1980, after Joy Division ended with Ian Curtis’s death. Surviving members Bernard Sumner, Peter Hook and Stephen Morris continued as a trio and were joined that October by keyboardist Gillian Gilbert. The new band’s debut single, “Ceremony,” a song written in Joy Division’s final weeks, appeared on Factory Records in January 1981. “Movement” followed that November, produced by Martin Hannett, who had also produced Joy Division’s two studio albums. The record marked the band’s transition from Curtis’s former group toward their own identity, mixing post-punk guitar work with the synthesisers and sequencers that would come to define their sound.

New Order’s next album, “Power, Corruption & Lies” (1983), pushed further into electronics, and its non-album single “Blue Monday” became the best-selling 12-inch single in UK chart history. “Low-Life” (1985) and “Brotherhood” (1986) continued to split guitar-driven and electronic material across their tracklists, and “Technique” (1989) and “Republic” (1993) carried the band through the end of Factory Records. Forty-five years after it introduced the group, “Movement” remains the first chapter of New Order’s catalogue.

items.title: Side-Line premieres Heimat’s new single ‘Mustard’
items.summary: Side-Line premieres "Mustard," the third single from Venice, Italy duo Heimat, out November 13, 2026 ahead of their debut EP.
items.fullText:
Side-Line premieres ‘”Mustard,”‘ the new single from Venice, Italy indie, post-punk and shoegaze duo Heimat, out November 13, 2026. It is the band’s third single, released ahead of their debut EP.

“Mustard” turns the frustration of a failed relationship into an upbeat, dance-driven track, built around sharp, tongue-in-cheek lyrics about an impossible-to-please ex, said Morgan Pettersson-Feret, who sings and writes lyrics in the band: “Mustard is one of those songs that just makes you wanna have fun and shake off a breakup. I had this poem written for a few months, an F-you to your ex sort of poem. I wasn’t sure how this idea would unfold until Gianluca showed me an idea for a song that he had titled ‘Mustard’ and I knew I had the perfect lyrics to accompany the start of this idea. In fact I had written about an ex who didn’t like mustard, and could never be satisfied with life, the relationship and with me. The song is a release of anger and emotions over a breakup through a more upbeat, dance style.”

Andrea Volpato recorded, mixed and mastered the single at his Fox Recording Studios, which operates between Seattle, Washington and Venice, Italy. Volpato also wrote and recorded the drums; Heimat’s Gianluca Favero and Pettersson-Feret wrote all guitar, bass, vocal and synthesizer parts themselves.

Heimat will perform at Oma Doris in Dortmund on November 20, 2026, opening for Sloe Noon, one week after the release of “Mustard.”

About Heimat

Heimat is a music project formed in Venice, Italy by Italian-born Gianluca Favero and Seattle-born Morgan Pettersson-Feret. Favero spent years touring Europe and the UK as bassist for MØAA, sharing stages with Yves Tumor and playing festivals including Ypsigrock in Sicily and MIL Lisbon, and also toured as guitarist for Painted Vein. Wanting to write his own songs, Favero joined forces with Pettersson-Feret, blending his shoegaze and post-punk sensibilities with her Seattle grunge roots and folk influences. “Mustard” is the project’s third single, arriving as the duo work toward their debut EP.

items.title: Johannes Groth announces new instrumental single ‘Beyond the Turn’
items.summary: Norwegian musician Johannes Groth releases the instrumental single "Beyond the Turn" on November 13 via DaWorks Records, with bassist Adam Neely.
items.fullText:
Norwegian musician, composer and producer Johannes Groth releases his new instrumental single “Beyond the Turn” today November 13 through DaWorks Records. The track combines progressive rock and fusion, built on shifting time signatures and contrasting atmospheres, and features a guest bass solo from Adam Neely.

Groth wrote, played and produced the track himself, handling guitars, keyboards and Hammond B3 alongside composition, production and mixing. Jeduthun Adesina plays drums and Martin Windstad percussion; Thomas Berg handled mastering. Groth has worked professionally as a musician and producer for 16 years, with a background in progressive metal and credits across several bands and projects alongside his own instrumental material.

“Beyond the Turn” follows a run of DaWorks Records singles that Groth has released roughly every few months since late 2024, among them “Procession,” “Flying or Falling?,” “Before All Things,” “Coin-OP,” “The Beginning of Wisdom” and “First Breath.” The series has been building toward Groth’s debut album.

Earlier in 2026, Groth spoke to Side-Line’s Britta Pirkko about growing up in a musical family. His father is Hans-Erik Groth, his late uncle was Jan Groth, and his cousins are Stephan Groth and Jonas Groth of Apoptygma Berzerk. The conversation also covered Groth’s collaborations with musicians including Larnell Lewis and Nate Werth, and his plans for the debut album.

‘Beyond the Turn’ credits

  • Johannes Groth: composition, guitars, keyboards, Hammond B3, production, mixing
  • Adam Neely: bass
  • Jeduthun Adesina: drums
  • Martin Windstad: percussion
  • Thomas Berg: mastering

About Johannes Groth

Johannes Groth is a Norwegian musician, composer and producer who has worked professionally in music for 16 years. He comes from a musical family: his father is Hans-Erik Groth, his late uncle was the artist Jan Groth, and his cousins Stephan Groth and Jonas Groth are members of Apoptygma Berzerk. Groth’s own background is in progressive metal, and he has contributed to various bands and projects while developing a parallel body of instrumental solo material.

Since late 2024, Groth has released a steady run of instrumental singles through DaWorks Records, including “Procession,” “Flying or Falling?,” “Before All Things,” “Coin-OP,” “The Beginning of Wisdom” and “First Breath,” building toward a debut album. His collaborators on these releases have included musicians such as Larnell Lewis and Nate Werth. Groth discussed his family background, his collaborations and his album plans in an interview with Side-Line earlier in 2026. “Beyond the Turn,” featuring a guest bass solo from Adam Neely, continues that release schedule on November 13 via DaWorks Records.

items.title: execunit releases ‘Activate’ single and video
items.summary: Swedish electronic act execunit releases the single and video "Activate," with a remix by Cryo, on Town And Towers Records, November 13.
items.fullText:
Swedish electronic act execunit releases the single and official music video ‘”Activate”‘ on November 13, 2026, through Town And Towers Records. The single comes with a remix by Cryo (Martin Rudefelt).

“Activate” is told from the perspective of artificial intelligence and its robotic followers, depicting the moment machines receive the order to begin taking control. Musically, the track departs from execunit’s earlier, darker material, drawing on 1990s alternative dance music for a more uplifting, dance-oriented sound. The accompanying video shows robots issuing the activation order, and features an execunit member transformed into a cyborg through AI-assisted video manipulation. Cryo’s remix takes the track in a different direction again, built around a 1980s-inspired dance sound.

“Activate” is available on major streaming services.

About execunit

execunit was initialized in 2022 by Andreas Rimheden, also known from the project Eternity Range and from Morticians, a dark electronic underground band from Sweden’s 1990s scene. Rimheden conceived execunit as a project that sounds like it was made by machines, for machines, with a mechanical, artificial lead vocal standing in for a machine priest or prophet. The project draws on dystopian science-fiction soundtracks by composers such as John Carpenter, the robotic music of Kraftwerk, and early industrial and Krautrock sounds.

execunit released the single “Rust” in March 2024 and the single “Humanicide” in June 2026, both on Town And Towers Records, followed by the album “Prophecy” in October 2026. “Activate” continues the project’s narrative of machines inheriting the world from their human creators.

items.title: “I Fear the Coldness of Machines” — Corlyx and Mark Gemini Thwaite Sing of a Bleak Future in Video for “Die Young”
items.summary: I fear the coldness of machines They’re building our death, and our disease And the world keeps falling apart The future has been canceled, the world has gone mad, and… The post “I Fear the Coldness of Machines” — Corlyx and Mark Gemini Thwaite Sing of a Bleak
items.fullText:
I fear the coldness of machines

They’re building our death,

and our disease

And the world keeps falling apart

The future has been canceled, the world has gone mad, and machines have inherited the asylum, while the kids watch civilization come apart, and the people responsible congratulate themselves on another profitable quarter. Somewhere amid this magnificent technological disaster, Corlyx have found a reason to turn up the guitars and contemplate the prospect of an early grave. Their new single, Die Young, featuring goth rock veteran Mark Gemini Thwaite of The Mission, Tricky, and Peter Murphy, takes the mounting anxieties of an increasingly disposable generation and puts them to work in a gloriously dramatic piece of death pop.

Originally formed in Los Angeles and now operating between the UK and Turin, Corlyx revolve around singer-songwriter Caitlin Stokes, guitarist and producer Brandon Ashley, bassist Davide Rocco, and drummer Flow Toulman. Their music has always enjoyed the theatrical possibilities of despair, and “Die Young” finds them contemplating a society where technological progress and collective extinction appear to be advancing at roughly the same speed.

Stokes sings of machines, manufactured disease, collapsing cities, and children frightened out of their minds by a future that increasingly resembles a particularly unpleasant science-fiction paperback. The repeated cries for help carry an awful implication: everyone is screaming, and nobody has the slightest idea who might come to the rescue. Her delivery moves between weary apprehension and full-throated alarm, giving the chorus the desperate energy of an entire generation discovering that the adults have misplaced the instruction manual.

Thwaite’s guitar playing brings considerable character to the proceedings. Drawing inspiration from John McGeoch, he introduces flamenco-style acoustic flourishes alongside his unmistakable electric guitar work, lending the arrangement an elegant, almost romantic tension. Those intricate touches sit beautifully against Corlyx’s muscular rhythms and sweeping melodies, with the song gathering momentum toward a chorus designed to send a crowded goth club into communal existential crisis.

“When Caitlin invited me to record some guitar ideas…in its demo stage, I was struck by the energy of the song and its post-punk atmosphere,” Thwaite recalls. “Looking forward to hearing it on the dancefloor!”

Directed by Stokes, the accompanying music video intercuts band performances with scenes of protest, ceremonial imagery, and visions of catastrophe drawn from the increasingly apocalyptic state of the modern world.

Watch below:

Released through Out Of Line Music, “Die Young” introduces The Crimson Tapes, Corlyx’s forthcoming 13-track album, due March 19, 2027. Following 2025’s sprawling Purple Pain, the record promises gothic literature, doomed lovers, Frankenstein’s monster, and enough romantic catastrophe to keep a Victorian cemetery fully occupied.

The apocalypse may be coming, but Corlyx have supplied an excellent reason to dance through the preliminary announcements. And with Thwaite aboard, the funeral procession has acquired one hell of a guitarist.

items.title: Baltimore Synth Punk trio Fun Never Starts crashes the Privilege Party in Video for “You Can’t Come”
items.summary: It’s all fine as long as I can goon To what Grok tells me Build a AI girlfriend Who will isolate me Civilization has reached the point where the people… The post Baltimore Synth Punk trio Fun Never Starts crashes the Privilege Party in Video for “You Can’t Com
items.fullText:
It’s all fine as long as I can goon
To what Grok tells me
Build a AI girlfriend Who will
isolate me

Civilization has reached the point where the people running the asylum have stopped bothering with disguises, the machines are writing love letters to lonely men, and the billionaires are throwing private parties while the rest of us contemplate a bleak future. Welcome to You Can’t Come, the latest exercise in organized social delinquency from Baltimore synthpunk trio Fun Never Starts, who have thoughtfully provided a soundtrack for the collapse of Western civilization. Bring your own disinfectant.

Comprised of Gashius Clay (production, bass, cello, vocals), Slim Dickens (guitar, illustration, puns), and Dwight Fried (vocals, synths, painting, lighting design), Fun Never Starts specialize in the sort of industrial-electronic misbehavior that might result if My Life with the Thrill Kill Kult, ADULT., and Peaches were locked overnight in a condemned nightclub. Their music inhabits the territory between post-punk, electroclash, and industrial rock, where the synthesizers sound mildly dangerous, the guitars have developed antisocial tendencies, and the rhythms suggest that dancing may be your final opportunity to exercise free will.

For You Can’t Come, the band have assembled a particularly unpleasant little aristocracy. Three characters dominate the proceedings: The Spy, a caricature of secretive wealth and influence; The Alpha, a send-up of authoritarian posturing and internet masculinity; and Sister Peligro, who personifies the use of religious authority to justify prejudice and social exclusion.

“We play alter egos of the people wrecking everything: a spy for the 1% who sneak around running the world, an alpha influencer pushing fascism to your feed, and a nun for those using religion to discriminate against those who need help most,” says Gashius Clay. “Then we turn on the AI execs who are gutting art and critical thinking.”

The video, directed by Dieinafire.org, presents these characters as a grotesque ruling class, presiding over a carnival of privilege, sexual excess, and institutional hypocrisy. Private clubs, luxurious mansions, and clandestine gatherings evoke the mythology of elite decadence, where the pursuit of pleasure becomes indistinguishable from the exercise of power. References to Bohemian Grove, secret societies, and the more extravagant conspiracy theories surrounding the wealthy provide plenty of material for the band’s particularly mischievous brand of social satire. Everybody wants admission to the party, yet nobody seems especially concerned about what happens once the doors are locked.

Comedian and seemingly prophet George Carlin articulated the membership policy years ago: “It’s a big club, and you ain’t in it.” In the band’s exaggerated vision, privilege becomes a private amusement park where the rules are written by those who can afford to ignore them. Outsiders are left to contemplate the absurdity of wanting admission to a club that seems determined to make everyone miserable. Even the promise of belonging comes with restrictions.

Watch the video for You Can’t Come below:

The song subsequently turns its attention to another contemporary anxiety: the increasingly intimate relationship between technology, entertainment, and human isolation. Artificial companions offer the simulation of affection, algorithms promise effortless answers, and the commercial enthusiasm surrounding generative AI raises uncomfortable questions about the future of creativity and independent thought. Fun Never Starts exaggerate these concerns into a particularly ridiculous vision of technological dependency, where loneliness becomes a business opportunity and even fantasy arrives courtesy of a corporate subscription.

Between the sexual grotesqueries, conspiratorial references, and synthetic intimacy, You Can’t Come imagines a civilization so thoroughly alienated that even its pleasures have become commodities.

Musically, Fun Never Starts make this nightmare surprisingly danceable. Their industrial machinery grinds against synthpunk irreverence, producing the sort of deranged nightclub entertainment that rewards bad judgment and punishes sobriety.

“You Can’t Come” is a filthy, funny satire of wealth, manufactured desire, technological dependency, and the peculiar human appetite for belonging to institutions that would rather keep us outside. The world’s going to hell, apparently, but at least somebody remembered to hire a band.
